examples.label: fstab - mount points and possible creds
Hidden files owned by the current user
OSCP Ch17 — show all mounted filesystems
OSCP Ch17 — all disks and partitions (spot unmounted drives)

notes: fstab can hold cleartext mount credentials; hidden dotfiles and world-writable temp dirs (/tmp, /dev/shm) are where dropped secrets and staging live. Always read /etc/fstab and hunt dotfiles before moving on. Also covered in: OSCP PEN-200 Chapter 17 (Linux Privilege Escalation).

recommended.note: Hunt configs/keys once you know the layout.

name: Enumeration - Filesystem, Mounts and Hidden Files
description: Inspect mounts and fstab (can contain credentials for network shares), block devices, temp dirs, and hidden files/dirs that often hold keys, configs, and history.

variations.label: Mounts / fstab
variations.command:
cat /etc/fstab
cat /etc/fstab | grep -v "#" | column -t
df -h
lsblk
lpstat

variations.label: Hidden files/dirs
variations.command:
find / -type f -name ".*" -exec ls -l {} \; 2>/dev/null | grep <user>
find / -type d -name ".*" -ls 2>/dev/null
ls -l /tmp /var/tmp /dev/shm
